Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Our results also showed that the BAS did not reduce factorially to one dimension, as has been found among Western samples (Avalos et al., 2005); rather, there was one dominant factor related to general body appreciation, which is consistent with work conducted among other non-Western samples (Swami, Campana, et al., 2011; Swami & Chamorro-Premuzic, 2008).

Assessment of BMI.evidence_source: In terms of weight discrepancy specifically, we found that Zimbabwean migrants in Britain had greater weight discrepancy than their peers in Zimbabwe, which seems to have been driven by the perception that they have larger body sizes (despite no significant between-group difference in self-reported BMI) and also seek to adopt a thinner ideal.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section compares body image and appreciation between Zimbabwean migrants in Britain and their counterparts in Zimbabwe, finding that migrants had more negative body image and greater weight discrepancy. The study used the BAS, which did not reduce factorially to one dimension in this non-Western sample. It also found that greater exposure to Western media was associated with lower body appreciation in both samples. The study, referred to as 'this study', involved two distinct samples: Zimbabwean women in Zimbabwe and Zimbabwean migrant women in Britain.
